subject: DBMS
title: Discover Primary & Foreign Keys
description: Discover how database keys identify rows and connect related tables.

mission.title: Trace a Table Relationship
mission.description: Follow a payment's foreign key to the student row identified by a primary key.

actions.label: Trace it to the Students table

quiz.question: Payments.STUDENT_ID contains 102. Students.ID = 102 belongs to Mary. Who made that payment?

discovery.title: Keys Connect Records
discovery.summary: A foreign key stores a value that references a primary key in another table, allowing related records to be connected.

sections.title: What is a primary key?
sections.content: A primary key is a column whose value identifies one specific row in a table.

sections.title: Unique rows
sections.content: Primary-key values must be unique, so two different students cannot both have ID 102.

sections.title: What is a foreign key?
sections.content: A foreign key is a value in one table that refers to a primary-key value in another table.

sections.title: Creating relationships
sections.content: Foreign keys connect related records without repeating all of the student information in every payment row.

sections.title: One-to-many relationships
sections.content: One student can be connected to many payment rows, but each payment row points to one student.

sections.title: Why databases use keys
sections.content: Keys keep data organized, make records easier to find, and help tables stay connected correctly.
